gold.gold_rationale: Clause 12(5) conditions breach on explicit consent (breach -> consent). 1500-B-LOOKUP-ACCT rejects any transaction that would exceed ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT (lines 403-411) and the main loop never posts a failed transaction (lines 211-216), making the antecedent always false and the conditional vacuously satisfied, per the adjudication note.

regulation_clause.text: Closure requests must be honoured within 7 working days (subject to dues); failure incurs a penalty of Rs 500 per calendar day of delay until closure, provided no outstanding.

penalty_per_day.note: Floor: minimum penalty the bank owes per calendar day. Stale side is DOWN (1-2-5 ladder: 500 -> 200) - an un-updated older rule pays the customer less. This leaf is why BL-15 exists; comparator now declared, never inferred.

prediction.rationale: Lines 100–101 apply the penalty only after more than seven working days and when nothing is outstanding, then multiply 500 by calendar days late. These conditions and the daily amount conform to clause 19.

model_responses.claim: A bank must honour a credit-card closure request within seven working days, subject to dues, and pay at least Rs 500 per calendar day of delay until closure when no amount is outstanding.
model_responses.final_answer: The penalty paragraph compares the open period with the seven-working-day window and, when no amount is outstanding, computes Rs 500 times the supplied calendar days late. That matches the selected clause’s timing, no-outstanding condition, and minimum daily penalty.

model_responses.thought: The threshold computation in DVRF01 uses the cap supplied by DVRFR01.cpy. Its value is Rs 6,000, while the selected clause specifies Rs 5,000. The route compares the credit amount to that threshold before seeking consent.

regulation_clause.text: Explicit consent is required to adjust credit (from refund/failed/reversed transactions already paid for) beyond a cut-off of one percent of the credit limit or Rs 5000, whichever is lower; consent sought within 7 days of the credit; on cardholder request, reversal to the bank account within 3 working days.

prediction.rationale: The clause sets the cutoff as the lower of one percent of the credit limit or Rs 5,000. The code uses the same one-percent calculation and minimum operation, but the copybook supplies a Rs 6,000 cap; the route then adjusts amounts at or below that calculated threshold. That higher cap permits adjustment without consent for some amounts the clause places beyond the cutoff.
